labs.title: Keep a value inside the rails
labs.prompt: Implement clamp(value, min, max). Return value bounded inclusively by min and max. All three arguments must be finite numbers, otherwise throw TypeError. If min exceeds max, throw RangeError. Do not coerce strings. Preserve zero and fractional values.
hints: Validate before computing the answer. Number.isFinite does not coerce strings.
A value below min becomes min; a value above max becomes max.
Compose Math.max(min, value) inside Math.min(max, ...).

tests.name: Reject invalid input
tests.code: for (const value of [NaN, Infinity, "2", null]) { let error; try { clamp(value, 0, 3); } catch(e) { error = e; } assert(error instanceof TypeError, "Reject non-finite numbers"); }

tests.name: Reject reversed bounds
tests.code: let error; try { clamp(1, 8, 2); } catch(e) { error = e; } assert(error instanceof RangeError, "Reversed bounds must fail");

labs.title: Convert temperature deliberately
labs.prompt: Implement convertTemperature(value, from, to), accepting only finite numeric values and the units C, F, K. Convert through Celsius and return a number rounded to two decimal places. Unknown units or non-finite values throw TypeError. A temperature below absolute zero throws RangeError, including when source and destination units match.
hints: Use Celsius as the intermediate representation.
Fahrenheit to Celsius is (F − 32) × 5 / 9. Kelvin to Celsius subtracts 273.15.
Round only the final answer, using Number(result.toFixed(2)).

tests.name: Impossible temperature
tests.code: let e; try { convertTemperature(-1, "K", "K"); } catch(x) { e = x; } assert(e instanceof RangeError, "Reject below zero Kelvin");

tests.name: No coercion or unknown units
tests.code: for (const args of [["4", "C", "F"], [4, "X", "C"], [NaN, "C", "F"]]) { let e; try { convertTemperature(...args); } catch(x) { e = x; } assert(e instanceof TypeError, "Invalid arguments must fail"); }

labs.title: Quote a basket in integer cents
labs.prompt: Implement quoteBasket(items, discountPercent = 0). Each item is {priceCents, quantity}, both non-negative safe integers. discountPercent must be an integer from 0 to 100. Return {subtotalCents, discountCents, totalCents}, rounding the discount to the nearest cent with Math.round. Invalid fields throw RangeError. Inputs will have safe-integer aggregate totals. Leave the input unchanged.
hints: Use integer cents throughout; do not convert to currency units.
Subtotal each line as priceCents × quantity, then apply one discount to the basket.

Split subtotalCents into whole hundreds and a remainder before multiplying by the percentage. Round only the remainder contribution: floor(subtotal / 100) × percent + round((subtotal % 100) × percent / 100). This avoids unsafe intermediate multiplication.

tests.name: Input remains intact
tests.code: const items = [{priceCents:101, quantity:2}]; const before = JSON.stringify(items); quoteBasket(items, 5); assertEqual(JSON.stringify(items), before);

tests.name: Invalid line rejected
tests.code: let e; try { quoteBasket([{priceCents:1.5, quantity:2}]); } catch(x) { e=x; } assert(e instanceof RangeError, "Reject fractional cents");

tests.name: Invalid discount rejected
tests.code: let e; try { quoteBasket([], 101); } catch(x) { e=x; } assert(e instanceof RangeError, "Reject excessive discount");

tests.name: Safe totals near the numeric limit

labs.title: The calendar edge case
labs.prompt: Implement daysInMonth(year, month). year is an integer from 1 through 9999; month is an integer from 1 through 12. Invalid arguments throw RangeError. Use Gregorian leap-year rules: divisible by 4, except centuries unless divisible by 400. Return the number of days without using Date.
hints: Separate input validation, leap-year detection, and month lookup.
A century such as 1900 is special, but 2000 passes the 400-year exception.
Index a twelve-element array with month - 1.

tests.name: Reject invalid range and types
tests.code: for (const args of [[0,1],[2024,13],[2024,0],[2024,2.5],["2024",2]]) { let e; try { daysInMonth(...args); } catch(x) { e=x; } assert(e instanceof RangeError, "Validate both calendar arguments"); }

labs.title: Price a progressive delivery route
labs.prompt: Implement deliveryFee(distanceKm, express = false). Finite distances greater than zero and up to 100 are allowed; otherwise throw RangeError. Charge 500 cents for the first 3 km, 120 cents for each started km after 3 through 10, then 80 cents for each started km beyond 10. Express adds 50% to the complete fee, rounded with Math.round. Return cents.
hints: Treat the journey as three independent distance bands.
Use Math.ceil for each started kilometer, after clipping to the band.
Apply the express multiplier after summing every distance band.

tests.name: Reject unsupported values
tests.code: for (const n of [0,-1,101,Infinity,"4"]) { let e; try { deliveryFee(n); } catch(x) {e=x;} assert(e instanceof RangeError, "Invalid route distance"); }

labs.title: Describe a password without storing it
labs.prompt: Implement passwordReport(text). Return {valid, missing}, where missing lists unmet rules in this exact order: length (at least 12 Unicode code points), lowercase (ASCII a-z), uppercase (ASCII A-Z), digit (ASCII 0-9), symbol (one of !@#$%^&*). Do not trim or otherwise transform text. valid is true exactly when no rules are missing. Assume text is a string. This exercise checks stated rules, not real-world password strength.
hints: Represent rules as ordered [name, passed] pairs.
Use [...text].length to count code points, since some characters use two UTF-16 code units.
Filter failed rules and derive valid from the resulting array length.

labs.title: Reduce a fraction with Euclid
labs.prompt: Implement reduceFraction(numerator, denominator). Both inputs are safe integers and denominator cannot be zero; otherwise throw RangeError. Return [n, d] in lowest terms with a positive denominator. Zero always becomes [0, 1]. Use the Euclidean algorithm rather than testing every possible divisor.
hints: Take absolute values while finding the greatest common divisor.
Repeatedly replace [a, b] with [b, a % b] until b is zero.
Normalize the sign only after dividing both inputs by the divisor.

tests.name: Invalid fractions
tests.code: for (const args of [[1,0],[1.5,2],[1,"2"]]) {let e; try {reduceFraction(...args);} catch(x) {e=x;} assert(e instanceof RangeError, "Invalid fraction must fail");}

labs.title: Build a directional range
labs.prompt: Implement integerRange(start, end, step = 1), returning an array that includes start and excludes end. Arguments must be safe integers and step must not be zero; otherwise throw RangeError. Positive steps move upward; negative steps move downward. A step pointing away from end returns an empty array. Inputs will produce at most 1000 values and will not overflow safe integers.
hints: The loop condition depends on the sign of step.
Exclude end even when the progression lands exactly on it.
A conditional expression in the loop condition can choose value < end or value > end.

tests.name: Guard termination
tests.code: let e; try {integerRange(1,5,0);} catch(x) {e=x;} assert(e instanceof RangeError,"Zero step must throw");

labs.title: Group records without prototype surprises
labs.prompt: Implement groupBy(items, keyOf). Return a Map from each callback-produced key to a new array of matching items, preserving first-seen key order and original item order. Call keyOf once per item with (item, index). Keys may be strings, objects, or undefined. Do not mutate items.
hints: A Map supports object keys and avoids special string property names.
Create an array when a key first appears, then append each item.
Pass the original array index to the callback, without changing the source array.

tests.name: Object identity keys
tests.code: const key={}; const a={key}; const b={key}; assertEqual(groupBy([a,b], x=>x.key).get(key), [a,b]);

tests.name: Callback index and count
tests.code: let calls=0; const result=groupBy(["a","b","c"],(x,i)=>{calls++;return i%2;}); assertEqual([...result], [[0,["a","c"]],[1,["b"]]]); assertEqual(calls,3);

labs.title: Deduplicate by a chosen identity
labs.prompt: Implement uniqueBy(items, keyOf), returning the first item for each distinct key. Use SameValueZero equality, as Set does: NaN equals NaN and 0 equals -0; object keys compare by identity. Preserve order, invoke keyOf(item, index) once per item, and return a new array without mutating the input.
hints: Track seen keys, rather than seen items.
A Set already implements the requested equality semantics.
A filter callback should add a previously unseen key and return true.

tests.name: NaN and signed zero
tests.code: const result=uniqueBy([NaN,NaN,0,-0],x=>x); assertEqual(result.length,2); assert(Number.isNaN(result[0]),"Keep first NaN");

tests.name: New array and callback count
tests.code: const source=[1,1,2]; let calls=0; const result=uniqueBy(source,(x,i)=>{assert(i>=0,"Pass index");calls++;return x;}); assert(result!==source,"Return new array"); assertEqual(calls,3); assertEqual(source,[1,1,2]);

labs.title: Build a word-frequency report
labs.prompt: Implement wordFrequencies(text). A word is a maximal sequence of ASCII letters a-z, case-insensitive; punctuation and digits are separators. Return an array of {word, count}, sorted by count descending, then word ascending using ordinary lexical comparison. Empty or punctuation-only input returns [].
hints: Extract ASCII letter sequences with /[A-Za-z]+/g first, then lowercase each token. Lowercasing all Unicode text first can turn non-ASCII symbols into ASCII letters.
Count with a Map, defaulting unseen words to zero.
Your comparator needs a deterministic secondary ordering when counts tie.

labs.title: Compose a small data pipeline
labs.prompt: Implement pipe(...functions). Validate every supplied value is a function when pipe is called; otherwise throw TypeError. Return a unary function applying the functions left to right. With no functions, return the input unchanged. Propagate exceptions and preserve object identity where a stage returns the same reference. This is a synchronous pipeline.
hints: The outer function captures a list of stages.
The inner function can reduce that list, starting with its own input.
Validate the stage list before returning the inner function, so invalid pipelines fail early.

tests.name: Identity pipeline
tests.code: const value={}; assert(pipe()(value)===value,"An empty pipeline preserves identity");

tests.name: Early validation
tests.code: let e; try {pipe(x=>x,42);} catch(x) {e=x;} assert(e instanceof TypeError,"Reject invalid stages immediately");

tests.name: Error propagation
tests.code: const expected=new Error("stop"); let e; try {pipe(()=>{throw expected;})(1);} catch(x) {e=x;} assert(e===expected,"Propagate original error");

labs.title: Memoize a single argument safely
labs.prompt: Implement memoizeUnary(fn), returning a wrapper that caches successful results by its single argument in a Map. Cache undefined and falsy results too. Preserve the calling this value when invoking fn; the cache key is only the argument, so assume the meaning of fn does not vary by receiver. Synchronous exceptions must not be cached. Object arguments use identity.

examples.input: const square = memoizeUnary(n => n * n); square(5)

hints: Use Map.has rather than truthiness of Map.get.
An ordinary function can forward this using fn.call(this, arg).
Set the cache after invoking fn; if fn throws, no entry will be written.

tests.name: Cache successful work
tests.code: let count=0; const twice=memoizeUnary(x=>{count++;return x*2;}); assertEqual([twice(3),twice(3),twice(4)],[6,6,8]); assertEqual(count,2);

tests.name: Cache undefined
tests.code: let count=0; const fn=memoizeUnary(()=>{count++;}); fn(1); fn(1); assertEqual(count,1);

tests.name: Exceptions are retried
tests.code: let count=0; const fn=memoizeUnary(()=>{count++;throw new Error("x");}); for(let i=0;i<2;i++){try{fn(1);}catch{}} assertEqual(count,2);

tests.name: Object identity
tests.code: let count=0; const fn=memoizeUnary(()=>++count); const key={}; assertEqual([fn(key),fn(key),fn({})],[1,1,2]);

labs.title: Flatten a nested settings object
labs.prompt: Implement flattenRecord(record), returning an array of [dotPath, value] pairs for leaves in Object.entries traversal order. Recurse into non-null plain objects only; arrays and null are leaves. Empty nested objects are leaves too. The root is always a plain object; an empty root returns []. Keys contain no dots but may be empty strings, and there are no cycles. Do not mutate the source.
hints: Keep the path as an array of key segments and join with dots only when emitting a leaf. This preserves empty-string keys.
Arrays should be emitted as a single leaf, not expanded into numeric paths.
An empty nested object needs its own leaf entry; otherwise that setting disappears.

tests.name: Empty keys retain their path position

labs.title: Apply a ledger without changing history
labs.prompt: Implement applyTransactions(balances, transactions). balances is a plain object of account IDs to non-negative integer cents; transactions are {from, to, amount}. Validate each amount is a positive safe integer and both accounts exist as own properties. Apply transactions in order to a fresh object. Insufficient funds throw RangeError; unknown accounts throw Error. Transfers to the same account still require sufficient funds but leave its balance unchanged. Never mutate either input, even if a later transfer fails.
hints: Copy balances before applying any transaction.
Check own properties rather than using the in operator.
Validate a transfer fully, then subtract and add; this also handles self-transfers.

tests.name: Failure does not mutate input
tests.code: const source={a:50,b:0}; let e; try{applyTransactions(source,[{from:"a",to:"b",amount:10},{from:"a",to:"b",amount:100}]);}catch(x){e=x;} assert(e instanceof RangeError,"Reject overdraft"); assertEqual(source,{a:50,b:0});

tests.name: Inherited account rejected
tests.code: let e; try{applyTransactions({a:50},[{from:"a",to:"toString",amount:1}]);}catch(x){e=x;} assert(e instanceof Error,"Reject inherited properties");

tests.name: Positive amounts only
tests.code: let e; try{applyTransactions({a:50,b:0},[{from:"a",to:"b",amount:0}]);}catch(x){e=x;} assert(e instanceof RangeError,"Reject zero transfer");

labs.title: Compute moving averages in one pass
labs.prompt: Implement movingAverage(values, size), returning the average of every complete consecutive window of size values. values must be a dense array of integers with absolute value at most 1,000,000,000. size must be an integer from 1 through 10,000. Invalid arguments or values throw RangeError. These bounds keep running sums exact safe integers; averages may be fractional JavaScript Numbers. If size exceeds the array length, return []. Validate all values even when no complete window exists. Do not mutate values. Aim for O(n) time with a running sum; do not sum each window from scratch.
hints: Validate the complete dense integer array and the window bounds before calculating. The stated bounds keep each running sum below Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER.
Track a running sum. Before adding the next value, subtract the old value if it is leaving the window.
Emit sum / size only after seeing size elements. Removing and adding one value per step gives O(n) time.

tests.name: Invalid size
tests.code: for(const size of [0,-2,1.5]){let e;try{movingAverage([1,2],size);}catch(x){e=x;}assert(e instanceof RangeError,"Validate window size");}

tests.name: Reject unsupported numeric inputs
tests.code: for(const values of [[1e16,1,1],[Number.MAX_VALUE],[0.5],[NaN],[Infinity],Array(1)]){let e;try{movingAverage(values,2);}catch(x){e=x;}assert(e instanceof RangeError,"Reject values outside the exact-sum domain");}let e;try{movingAverage([1],10001);}catch(x){e=x;}assert(e instanceof RangeError,"Enforce window bound");

labs.title: An undoable counter with private history
labs.prompt: Implement createCounter(initial = 0). Return {value, add, undo, reset}, where value() reads the current number, add(delta) records the old value then adds a finite number and returns the new value, undo() restores the most recent recorded value (or leaves the value unchanged if none), and reset() restores initial and clears history. initial and delta must be finite numbers or throw TypeError. Each instance must have independent private state.
hints: Keep current and history in the factory closure.
Record the previous value only after validating an addition.
Reset must clear history; otherwise undo could resurrect an old session.

tests.name: Invalid addition leaves state
tests.code: const c=createCounter(4); let e;try{c.add(NaN);}catch(x){e=x;} assert(e instanceof TypeError,"Reject invalid delta"); assertEqual(c.value(),4); assertEqual(c.undo(),4);

labs.title: A predictable event bus
labs.prompt: Implement createEventBus() returning on(event, listener), emit(event, payload), and listenerCount(event). on adds a function once per event and returns an idempotent unsubscribe function. Duplicate on calls for an active listener return the same disposer. Once disposed, that disposer must never remove a later re-subscription of the same listener. emit invokes a snapshot of listeners in registration order and returns the invocation count; changes to subscriptions during emission only affect future emissions. Listener errors propagate immediately. Unknown events have zero listeners.
hints: Map each event to an insertion-ordered Map of listener functions to their disposer functions.
Copy the listener keys into an array before emitting, so subscription changes do not change the current snapshot.
A disposer tracks whether its registration is still active. Return the existing disposer for a duplicate subscription; a fresh subscription after disposal gets a fresh disposer.

tests.name: Unknown events and errors
tests.code: const bus=createEventBus();assertEqual(bus.emit("missing",1),0);const expected=new Error("listener");bus.on("x",()=>{throw expected;});let e;try{bus.emit("x");}catch(x){e=x;}assert(e===expected,"Preserve listener error");

tests.name: Stale disposers cannot remove a new subscription
tests.code: const bus=createEventBus(),fn=()=>{};const first=bus.on("x",fn),duplicate=bus.on("x",fn);assert(first===duplicate,"Duplicate registration shares its disposer");first();const second=bus.on("x",fn);first();duplicate();assertEqual(bus.listenerCount("x"),1);second();assertEqual(bus.listenerCount("x"),0);

labs.title: Reserve stock as a small domain model
labs.prompt: Implement class Inventory with constructor(initial), available(sku), reserve(sku, quantity), restock(sku, quantity), and snapshot(). initial is a record of SKU to non-negative integer stock. reserve and restock require a known own-property SKU and a positive integer quantity, otherwise throw RangeError. reserve throws RangeError if insufficient stock. Both methods return the remaining quantity. available returns undefined for unknown SKUs. snapshot returns an independent plain object. Initial stock must also be validated.
hints: Copy and validate initial before storing it.
Use a private field to keep callers from bypassing validation.
Return a copy from snapshot, and distinguish unknown keys from stock equal to zero.

tests.name: Unknown and invalid quantities
tests.code: const stock=new Inventory({book:0});assert(stock.available("toString")===undefined,"Own keys only");for(const args of [["missing",1],["book",0],["book",1.5]]){let e;try{stock.restock(...args);}catch(x){e=x;}assert(e instanceof RangeError,"Validate operation");}

labs.title: Model a request lifecycle explicitly
labs.prompt: Implement transitionRequest(state, event). States are idle, loading, success, and error. Allowed transitions: idle + FETCH → loading; loading + RESOLVE → success; loading + REJECT → error; success/error + FETCH → loading; any known state + RESET → idle. Return a state string. Every unsupported state/event pair throws Error. The function must have no hidden mutable state.
hints: Represent the allowed pairs directly in a transition table.
Validate both the state key and the event key as own properties.
RESET should be present for every known state, but not for unknown states.

tests.name: Illegal transitions
tests.code: for(const pair of [["idle","RESOLVE"],["loading","FETCH"],["missing","RESET"],["idle","toString"]]){let e;try{transitionRequest(...pair);}catch(x){e=x;}assert(e instanceof Error,"Reject unsupported transition");}

labs.title: Freeze a cyclic object graph
labs.prompt: Implement deepFreeze(value). Recursively freeze objects and arrays reachable through own data properties, including non-enumerable and symbol properties. Return the same root reference. Handle cycles without infinite recursion. Primitive values and functions are returned unchanged. Do not invoke getters; freeze their containing object while leaving the getter function untouched. Input graphs contain only ordinary objects, arrays, primitive values, and functions; exotic built-ins such as typed arrays, Maps, and Sets are outside this exercise.
hints: Track visited objects in a WeakSet before descending.
Reflect.ownKeys includes symbols and non-enumerable property names.
Read property descriptors; descriptor.value is safe, while current[key] could execute a getter.

tests.name: Symbol and hidden data
tests.code: const symbol=Symbol();const root={[symbol]:{}};Object.defineProperty(root,"hidden",{value:{}});deepFreeze(root);assert(Object.isFrozen(root[symbol])&&Object.isFrozen(root.hidden),"Visit every own data property");

labs.title: Make failure an explicit value
labs.concept: Result types · function composition · error handling
labs.prompt: Implement attempt(fn) and mapResult(result, transform). attempt calls a zero-argument synchronous function and returns {ok:true,value} or {ok:false,error}, preserving a thrown value exactly. mapResult leaves failed results unchanged by reference; successful values pass through transform using attempt, so a thrown transform becomes a failed result. No promises are involved.

examples.output: A failed Result containing the parse error

hints: A try/catch can turn either branch into a tagged object.
The ok field distinguishes success even when the value is undefined.
For a failed result, return the original object without calling transform.

tests.name: Short-circuit failure
tests.code: const failed={ok:false,error:"first"};let called=false;assert(mapResult(failed,()=>{called=true;})===failed,"Return same failure");assert(!called,"Do not invoke transform");

labs.title: Merge settings with explicit rules
labs.prompt: Implement mergeSettings(base, override). Inputs are JSON-compatible plain objects with no cycles or dangerous property names. Recursively merge when both values at a key are non-null plain objects. Otherwise the override value replaces the base value, including arrays and null. Deep-copy all objects and arrays in the result so no mutable references are shared with either input. Preserve keys that only occur in base.
hints: Write a clone helper before writing the merge step.
Recurse only when both values are plain objects; arrays are replacement values.
Cloning untouched base branches is necessary to satisfy the no-shared-references contract.

labs.title: Keep an undoable history of snapshots
labs.prompt: Implement createHistory(initial). JSON-compatible snapshots must be copied on storage and read. Return current(), commit(value), undo(), redo(). commit replaces the redo branch and returns the stored value as a copy. undo and redo move one step when possible, otherwise remain at their boundary; both return a copy of the current snapshot. History starts with initial. Use structuredClone for copying.
hints: Keep an array of snapshots and an index into that array.
When committing after undo, discard entries after the current index.
Clone both incoming values and returned values to protect historical snapshots.

labs.title: Create a reusable lazy number sequence
labs.prompt: Implement rangeIterable(start, end, step = 1). Return a reusable iterable producing start inclusive to end exclusive. Accept safe integers only and reject zero step with RangeError, at factory-call time. Positive and negative steps are allowed; wrong-direction ranges are empty. Each iteration starts afresh. Do not create an array of the full range. Test inputs do not overflow safe integers.
hints: The factory should validate immediately, before returning an iterable.
Return an object whose Symbol.iterator method is a generator.
A fresh generator per iteration makes the iterable reusable.

labs.title: Chunk any iterable lazily
labs.prompt: Implement chunked(iterable, size), returning an iterable of arrays of at most size elements. The final partial chunk must be emitted. Validate size is a positive integer at factory-call time, otherwise throw RangeError. Consume the source only as output is requested. If the consumer stops early, close the source iterator through normal iterator cleanup. Strings, Sets, and generators must work.
hints: A generator can collect one chunk, yield it, then start a new array.
Use for...of inside the generator so early termination closes the underlying iterator.
Place validation outside the generator body to make it happen immediately.

tests.name: Laziness and closing
tests.code: let read=0,closed=false;function* source(){try{for(let n=0;n<10;n++){read++;yield n;}}finally{closed=true;}}const iterator=chunked(source(),2)[Symbol.iterator]();assertEqual(read,0);assertEqual(iterator.next().value,[0,1]);assertEqual(read,2);iterator.return();assert(closed,"Close source on early return");

labs.title: Limit asynchronous work without losing order
labs.prompt: Implement async mapLimit(items, limit, mapper). Run at most limit mapper calls simultaneously, passing (item, index). Return results in input order even when work finishes out of order. limit must be a positive integer or reject with RangeError. Propagate a mapper rejection. Empty input returns []. Do not mutate items. Once a rejection has been observed, workers must not schedule new items; already-running work may finish.

examples.input: await mapLimit([2,3,4], 2, async n => n * n)

hints: Use a shared next index and a fixed number of worker functions.
Each worker claims an index before awaiting; JavaScript executes that claim synchronously.
Store output by the claimed index, and set a shared failure flag before rethrowing.

tests.name: Concurrency bounded
tests.code: let active=0,max=0;const result=await mapLimit([1,2,3,4,5],2,async n=>{active++;max=Math.max(max,active);await Promise.resolve();await Promise.resolve();active--;return n*2;});assertEqual(result,[2,4,6,8,10]);assertEqual(max,2);

tests.name: Empty and invalid limit
tests.code: assertEqual(await mapLimit([],2,()=>0),[]);let e;try{await mapLimit([1],0,x=>x);}catch(x){e=x;}assert(e instanceof RangeError,"Reject invalid limit");

tests.name: Propagate error and stop scheduling
tests.code: const expected=new Error("fail");const called=[];let e;try{await mapLimit([1,2,3],1,async n=>{called.push(n);throw expected;});}catch(x){e=x;}assert(e===expected,"Preserve original rejection");assertEqual(called,[1]);

labs.title: Collect outcomes without short-circuiting
labs.prompt: Implement async settleAll(values) without using Promise.allSettled. values is an array whose entries may be promises, thenables, or ordinary values. Treat sparse array holes as undefined values. Return an ordered array of {status:"fulfilled", value} or {status:"rejected", reason}. One rejection must not discard the other outcomes. Preserve rejection reasons exactly, and resolve an empty input to [].
hints: Use Array.from(values, mapper) to visit every array position, including holes as undefined. Normalize each visited value with Promise.resolve.
Attach both success and rejection handlers, each returning an outcome object.
Promise.all can now collect those normalized outcomes because the wrappers fulfill.

tests.name: Identity of reasons
tests.code: const reason={code:9}; const rejected=Promise.reject(reason); rejected.catch(()=>{}); const results=await settleAll([rejected]); assert(results[0].reason===reason,"Preserve reason identity");

tests.name: Sparse array holes have fulfilled outcomes

labs.title: Retry with an injectable waiting strategy
labs.concept: Async control flow · dependency injection · backoff
labs.prompt: Implement async retry(operation, {attempts = 3, delay = async () => {}, shouldRetry = () => true} = {}). Call operation(attemptNumber), starting at 1. Return its first successful result. On failure, stop if attempts are exhausted or shouldRetry(error, attemptNumber) is false; rethrow the last error unchanged. Otherwise await delay(attemptNumber) before trying again. attempts must be a positive integer or reject with RangeError. A failure in delay or shouldRetry propagates immediately.

examples.input: await retry(async attempt => { if (attempt < 2) throw "busy"; return 42; })

hints: A for loop is often clearer than a recursive promise chain.
Only wait after a retryable failure with attempts remaining.
Keep the delay outside a new retry-catching region so delay failures do not trigger another operation.

tests.name: Success after retries
tests.code: const calls=[],waits=[];const value=await retry(async n=>{calls.push(n);if(n<3)throw new Error("transient");return "ok";},{delay:async n=>waits.push(n)});assertEqual(value,"ok");assertEqual(calls,[1,2,3]);assertEqual(waits,[1,2]);

tests.name: Stop on non-retryable error
tests.code: const expected=new Error("permanent");let calls=0,e;try{await retry(()=>{calls++;throw expected;},{shouldRetry:()=>false});}catch(x){e=x;}assert(e===expected,"Preserve error");assertEqual(calls,1);

tests.name: Exhaustion and invalid attempts
tests.code: let calls=0,e;try{await retry(()=>{calls++;throw "last";},{attempts:2});}catch(x){e=x;}assertEqual(e,"last");assertEqual(calls,2);let invalid;try{await retry(()=>1,{attempts:0});}catch(x){invalid=x;}assert(invalid instanceof RangeError,"Reject zero attempts");

labs.title: Implement a tiny LRU cache
labs.prompt: Implement createLRU(capacity), where capacity is a positive integer or throw RangeError. Return get(key), set(key, value), has(key), and keys(). A successful get refreshes recency, even for an undefined value. set refreshes existing keys and evicts the least-recently-used key when over capacity. has does not refresh recency. keys returns a new array ordered oldest to newest. Missing get returns undefined; set returns the stored value.

examples.input: const c = createLRU(1); c.set("a",1); c.set("b",2); c.keys()

hints: Map preserves insertion order.
Deleting and reinserting a key moves it to the newest position.
Use has before get so stored undefined remains distinguishable from a missing entry.

labs.title: Find the next UTC weekday
labs.prompt: Implement nextWeekdayUTC(isoDate, weekday). Accept only canonical UTC ISO strings in the exact format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ (four-digit years 0000–9999), with a real calendar date and time. weekday must be an integer 0 (Sunday) through 6 (Saturday). Invalid arguments throw RangeError. Return the next strictly later occurrence of that weekday in the same canonical format, preserving UTC time of day and milliseconds. If already on that weekday, advance seven days. Throw RangeError if the result would leave the supported four-digit year range. Use UTC operations so local daylight-saving time cannot change the result.
hints: Validate the exact canonical format before constructing Date. Compare date.toISOString() with the input to reject silent calendar rollover such as February 30.
Find the forward weekday distance with modular arithmetic; zero means seven days because the result must be strictly later.
Use getUTCDay and setUTCDate. Preserve milliseconds, then reject a result outside the supported four-digit year range.

tests.name: Reject invalid arguments
tests.code: for(const args of [["bad",1],["2024-01-01",7],["2024-01-01",1.5]]){let e;try{nextWeekdayUTC(...args);}catch(x){e=x;}assert(e instanceof RangeError,"Validate date and weekday");}

tests.name: Reject calendar rollover and noncanonical timestamps
tests.code: for(const value of ["2024-02-30T12:00:00.000Z","2023-02-29T12:00:00.000Z","12/31/2024","2024-01-01","2024-01-01T00:00:00Z","2024-01-01T24:00:00.000Z",null,Symbol("date")]){let e;try{nextWeekdayUTC(value,1);}catch(x){e=x;}assert(e instanceof RangeError,"Reject invalid or noncanonical timestamp");}

labs.title: Serialize BigInt through a tagged boundary
labs.prompt: Implement encodeBigInts(value) and decodeBigInts(text). Encode BigInt values as objects with exactly one key "$bigint" and a decimal string value. Decode only such single-key objects whose string matches /^-?(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$/. Other objects remain ordinary objects. Inputs are otherwise JSON-compatible, without cycles. The marker shape is reserved for BigInts: explain to yourself why this creates a collision boundary for ordinary user data.
hints: JSON.stringify accepts a replacer that transforms values before serialization.
JSON.parse accepts a reviver that transforms parsed children before their parent.
Check the exact object shape and decimal grammar before calling BigInt.

labs.title: Normalize a catalog URL query
labs.prompt: Implement parseCatalogQuery(search). Use URLSearchParams to return {q, page, tags}. q is the first q parameter trimmed, defaulting to "". page is the first page parameter if it contains only decimal digits and represents a positive safe integer, otherwise 1. tags collects every tag parameter, trimmed and lowercased, discarding empty strings and duplicates while preserving order. Unknown parameters are ignored. Plus signs and percent escapes follow URLSearchParams decoding.
hints: URLSearchParams handles decoding and repeated keys.
parseInt alone would incorrectly accept 2oops.
Normalize tags before deduplicating them.

labs.title: Paginate with stable boundary behavior
labs.prompt: Implement paginate(items, requestedPage, pageSize). Both numeric arguments must be positive integers or throw RangeError. Return {items, page, pageSize, totalItems, totalPages, hasPrevious, hasNext}. Clamp requestedPage to the last available page. Empty collections use page 1, totalPages 0, and false navigation flags. Return a new items array without mutating the source.
hints: Compute totalPages before clamping the requested page.
Use one as the minimum current page even when totalPages is zero.
Slice from (page - 1) × pageSize through page × pageSize.

tests.name: Immutability and validation
tests.code: const input=Object.freeze([1,2]);assert(paginate(input,1,10).items!==input,"Return new array");let e;try{paginate([],0,2);}catch(x){e=x;}assert(e instanceof RangeError,"Validate page");

labs.title: Validate a signup form deterministically
labs.prompt: Implement validateSignup(form), returning {valid, values, errors}. values is {name, email}: trim name and trim/lowercase email, treating non-strings as "". errors is ordered: {field:"name",code:"required"} for empty name, or code "too_long" for more than 60 Unicode code points; {field:"email",code:"invalid"} unless email matches /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/; {field:"terms",code:"required"} unless form.terms === true. valid means no errors. Leave form unchanged. This is a UI exercise, not comprehensive email validation.
hints: Normalize once, then validate normalized values.
Build errors in the requested field order.
Use a strict boolean check for terms.

labs.title: Rank a small local search index
labs.prompt: Implement searchDocuments(documents, query). Documents have unique string id, title, and body. Tokenize text into lowercase ASCII letter sequences and deduplicate query tokens. Results must contain every query token in title or body. Score each title occurrence as 3 and body occurrence as 1. Return {id, score} sorted by score descending then id lexically ascending. Tokenless queries return []. Do not modify documents.
hints: Use the same tokenizer for documents and queries: extract /[A-Za-z]+/g first, then lowercase each token. Non-ASCII characters remain separators.
Build weighted token counts for each document.
Deduplicate query tokens so repeated words do not inflate scores.

labs.title: Reduce a cart with structural sharing
labs.prompt: Implement cartReducer(state, action). state is an array of {id, quantity}. ADD with id and positive integer quantity appends or increments. SET with existing id and non-negative integer quantity replaces quantity; zero removes. REMOVE deletes an existing id. CLEAR empties the cart. Unknown actions and missing IDs for SET/REMOVE return original state. Invalid ADD/SET quantities throw RangeError. Changes return a new array and preserve unchanged item references. Same-value SET and CLEAR of empty state return original state. Never mutate state.
hints: Identify no-ops before allocating replacements.
Map only changed items to new objects.
Validate quantity before applying ADD or SET.

labs.title: Calculate a virtual list window
labs.prompt: Implement virtualWindow({count, rowHeight, viewportHeight, scrollTop, overscan = 0}). count and overscan are non-negative integers; rowHeight and viewportHeight are finite positive numbers; scrollTop is finite. Otherwise throw RangeError. Clamp scrollTop to [0, max(0, count * rowHeight - viewportHeight)]. Return {start, end, offsetTop, totalHeight}, covering visible rows plus overscan, with start inclusive and end exclusive. Empty lists return zeros. Use no DOM.
hints: Clamp scrolling before calculating indices.
Floor the first visible row and ceil the exclusive end.
Expand by overscan and clamp to available rows.

labs.title: Deduplicate requests only while pending
labs.prompt: Implement createInFlightCache(loader), returning load(key). Concurrent calls with the same key return the exact same Promise and invoke loader once. Remove the entry after settlement so a later call invokes loader again. Convert synchronous throws to rejected promises. Preserve results and rejection identity. Map key equality applies. Do not permanently cache successes or failures.
hints: An async wrapper would change the returned promise identity.
Promise.resolve().then captures synchronous loader throws.
Register cleanup on both fulfillment and rejection.

tests.name: Share pending promise
tests.code: let calls=0;const load=createInFlightCache(async key=>{calls++;return key+"!";});const a=load("x"),b=load("x");assert(a===b,"Share promise identity");assertEqual(await a,"x!");assertEqual(calls,1);

tests.name: Rejections are evicted
tests.code: const expected=new Error("offline");let calls=0;const load=createInFlightCache(()=>{calls++;throw expected;});let e;try{await load("x");}catch(x){e=x;}assert(e===expected,"Preserve error");try{await load("x");}catch{}assertEqual(calls,2);

labs.title: Project pending edits over server data
labs.prompt: Implement projectOptimistic(serverItems, operations). Items have unique string IDs. Operations are {type:"upsert", item} or {type:"remove", id}. Start with a deep copy of serverItems. Upsert completely replaces an existing item at its position, or appends a new item. Remove deletes a matching ID; unknown IDs do nothing. Apply in order. Unknown operation types throw TypeError. Return an array sharing no mutable references with inputs. structuredClone is available.
hints: Copy the server snapshot before applying edits.
Replacement keeps position; insertion appends.
Clone operation items too, avoiding another mutation path.

labs.title: Tokenize an arithmetic language
labs.prompt: Implement tokenizeExpression(source), returning tokens {type, value, start}. Types: "number", "operator", "paren". Numbers accept one or more digits optionally followed by a dot and one or more digits; their values are Numbers. Operators + - * / and parentheses ( ) have string values. Ignore whitespace. Unary signs are separate operators. Unsupported characters throw SyntaxError with their zero-based offset in its message. Do not evaluate source or use eval.
hints: Keep a cursor in the original string for accurate offsets.
Anchor number matching at the cursor and advance by the whole match.
Interpreting unary minus belongs to a parser; emit a minus token here.

labs.title: Order build tasks by dependency
labs.prompt: Implement orderTasks(graph). graph maps task names to dependency arrays. Return every task once, dependencies before consumers. Visit roots in Object.keys order and dependencies left to right with depth-first traversal for deterministic output. Missing dependencies throw Error. Cycles throw Error with "cycle" in the message. Do not mutate graph. Use own-property checks.
hints: Track both the current recursion path and completed tasks.
Append a task only after visiting its dependencies.
A task already on the recursion path reveals a cycle.

labs.title: Render a deliberately limited text template
labs.prompt: Implement renderTemplate(template, data). Replace {{ user.name }} placeholders using own properties only. Path segments match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*, separated by dots; whitespace is allowed only around the entire path. Missing, null, and undefined become "". Other values use String(value), escaped for HTML text: & < > double quote and apostrophe become & < > " and '. Malformed placeholders remain unchanged. This helper is for HTML text content only, never script, style, or URL contexts.
hints: Match only the specified placeholder grammar.
Check Object.hasOwn at every path segment.
Escape the final string once using a five-character replacement map.

labs.title: Protect a record with a validating proxy
labs.prompt: Implement createValidatedRecord(initial, validators). Both inputs have the same string keys; validators are functions returning booleans. Validate initial values, then return a Proxy over a shallow copy. Assignments to known keys must pass validation. Unknown keys or failed validation throw TypeError without changing state. Deleting or Object.defineProperty also throws TypeError. Reads are normal. Values are primitives. Validator exceptions propagate.

examples.output: Assignment succeeds; negative counts throw TypeError

hints: Validate initial state before exposing it.
Reflect.set on the raw target avoids triggering your own defineProperty trap.
Deletion and property definition need their own traps.

tests.name: Invalid assignment atomicity
tests.code: const r=createValidatedRecord({age:20},{age:n=>typeof n==="number"});let e;try{r.age="21";}catch(x){e=x;}assert(e instanceof TypeError,"Reject invalid value");assertEqual(r.age,20);

tests.name: Bypass paths blocked
tests.code: const r=createValidatedRecord({x:1},{x:Number.isFinite});for(const action of [()=>{r.y=2;},()=>{delete r.x;},()=>Object.defineProperty(r,"x",{value:9})]){let e;try{action();}catch(x){e=x;}assert(e instanceof TypeError,"Reject bypass");}assertEqual(r.x,1);

labs.title: Diff JSON records into deterministic patches
labs.concept: Tree comparison · JSON Pointer · deterministic output
labs.prompt: Implement diffJSON(before, after), returning operations {op:"add"|"remove"|"replace", path, value?}. Recurse when both values are non-null plain objects, visiting the sorted union of keys. Missing keys emit add/remove. Arrays are atomic: emit one replace if their JSON structure differs. Changed primitives/types emit replace. Root replacement uses path "". Escape each JSON Pointer segment: ~ to ~0 and / to ~1. Inputs are JSON-compatible without cycles. Deep-copy emitted values. Equivalent objects compare equal regardless of key insertion order.
hints: Separate structural equality from patch generation.
Visit a sorted union of keys for stable ordering.
Escape path segments individually and clone emitted values.

labs.title: Migrate versioned data without rewriting history
labs.concept: Schema evolution · pure boundaries · defensive copies
labs.prompt: Implement migrateRecord(record, migrations, targetVersion = migrations.length). record is {version, data}; migrations[i] upgrades version i to i+1 and returns new data. Validate integer versions with 0 <= record.version <= targetVersion <= migrations.length, otherwise throw RangeError. Deep-copy initial data before running migrations, which may mutate their input. Run required migrations in order and return {version:targetVersion, data}. Propagate errors. Leave original record unchanged even on failure.
hints: The stored version indexes the next migration.
Clone before any migration can mutate the data.
A no-op migration still returns independent data.

labs.title: Parse environment configuration at one boundary
labs.prompt: Implement parseEnvironment(env, schema). schema maps keys to {type:"string"|"number"|"boolean", required?:boolean, default?:value}. Read only own env keys. Absent keys and empty-string values use an own default if present, otherwise required fields add "KEY: required" and optional fields are omitted. Present nonempty values must be strings; an own property with value undefined is invalid rather than absent. Strings are preserved. Numbers use Number after rejecting whitespace-only strings and must be finite. Booleans accept exactly "true" or "false". Invalid values add "KEY: invalid TYPE". Ignore unknown env keys. Return {values, errors} in schema key order. Defaults are already correctly typed.
hints: Use Object.hasOwn to distinguish an absent key from a present value of undefined. Only absent keys and empty strings use defaults.
Boolean("false") is true; use explicit string comparisons.
Aggregate errors so all invalid settings can be fixed together.

tests.name: Aggregate failures
tests.code: assertEqual(parseEnvironment({N:"Infinity",B:"yes",S:42},{N:{type:"number"},B:{type:"boolean"},S:{type:"string"}}),{values:{},errors:["N: invalid number","B: invalid boolean","S: invalid string"]});

tests.name: Do not coerce non-string objects
tests.code: const raw={valueOf(){throw new Error("Do not coerce");}};assertEqual(parseEnvironment({N:raw},{N:{type:"number"}}),{values:{},errors:["N: invalid number"]});

tests.name: Present undefined does not use a default

labs.title: Build the smallest useful async test runner
labs.concept: Async execution · error reporting · deterministic tools
labs.prompt: Implement async runChecks(checks). Checks are {name, run}; run can return, fulfill, throw, or reject. Execute sequentially in order and continue after failures. Return {passed, failed, results}. Results are {name, status:"passed"} or {name, status:"failed", error}. Error objects use their message; other thrown values use String(value). Any normal return including false passes: assertions must throw to fail. Empty input returns zero counts and empty results. Never mutate checks.
hints: Use for...of with await to keep execution sequential.
Catch inside the loop so later checks still execute.
Convert thrown values to serializable text.

tests.name: Sequential execution
tests.code: const order=[];await runChecks([{name:"a",run:async()=>{order.push("start a");await Promise.resolve();order.push("end a");}},{name:"b",run:()=>order.push("b")}]);assertEqual(order,["start a","end a","b"]);
